MUJAHID:v2p555#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p555#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p555#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says night rolls over day and day rolls over night.

MUQATIL:39:4-5/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:4-5/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:4-5/r3.claim: God created heaven and earth with purpose, not in vain; He makes night and day take from one another and subjugated sun and moon for people.

MUQATIL:39:4-5/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:4-5/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:4-5/r4.claim: Sun and moon run until the Resurrection; their workings display God's oneness, might in dominion, and forgiveness for the repentant.

MAJAZ:v2p188/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p188/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p188/r1.claim: Yukawwiru al-layla ʿalā al-nahār means He brings night into day; its figure is yūliju, He inserts.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#2/r1.claim: Qatada explains the alternating night and day as one covering the other and each decreasing the other.

TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r1.claim: God rolls night over day and day over night, each covering the other, as in the verse saying he makes night enter day and day enter night.

TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says night is carried over day.

TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses “yukawwir” as rolling or coiling.

TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r4.claim: Qatada says each of night and day covers the other.

TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī describes day arriving as night departs, then night arriving as day departs.

TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p159#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd likewise says night goes and day covers it, then day goes and night covers it.

TAB-FULL:v20p161/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p161/r1.claim: God subjected sun and moon to help people count years, keep time, distinguish night from day, and manage their livelihoods.

TAB-FULL:v20p161/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p161/r2.claim: Sun and moon run until the Hour, when the sun is rolled up and the stars become dim; another view says each has a fixed orbit it cannot exceed or fall short of.

TAB-FULL:v20p161/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p161/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p161/r3.claim: God is mighty in vengeance against his enemies and forgiving toward servants who repent to him.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3248/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3248/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3248/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses God's folding the night over the day as the night carrying it.

NAHHAS:v4p3/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p3/r8.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v4p3/r8.claim: He explains the alternation of night and day as one being wrapped over the other; the author says this is the basic sense of takwīr.

NAHHAS:v4p3/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p3/r9.claim: He also says what is lost from night enters day and what is lost from day enters night.

THALABI:v8p221#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p221#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p221#3/r1.claim: Qatada explains the night covering the day and the day covering the night as each overlaying the other, like 7:54.

THALABI:v8p221#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p221#3/r2.speaker: المؤرخ
THALABI:v8p221#3/r2.claim: The historian glosses the alternating night and day as each entering into the other, paralleling 31:29.

THALABI:v8p221#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p221#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v8p221#3/r3.claim: Mujahid gives the concise interpretation that the night and day revolve.

THALABI:v8p221#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p221#3/r4.speaker: الحسن وابن حيان والكلبي
THALABI:v8p221#3/r4.claim: Hasan, Ibn Hayyan, and al-Kalbi say night diminishes as day lengthens and vice versa, with a stated maximum difference of nine and fifteen hours.

THALABI:v8p221#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p221#3/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p221#3/r5.claim: The root sense of takwīr is to roll and gather, as in winding a turban.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r1.claim: Takwir means night is carried over day and day over night.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r2.claim: Night covers day and removes its light, and day covers night and removes its darkness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r3.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r3.claim: One decreases as the other increases.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p114/r4.claim: Another possibility is night gathers until day spreads and day gathers until night spreads.

QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r4.claim: God created the heavens and earth rightly, and night and day enter into one another as they lengthen and shorten.

QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p112/r5.claim: The alternation of day and night also signifies the servant's changing states: contraction and expansion, union and separation, sobriety and ecstasy, doubt and connection.

JISHUMI:v8p6033/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6033/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6033/r6.claim: Takwir is wrapping or rolling, as with winding a turban; ajal is a set time.

JISHUMI:v8p6037/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6037/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6037/r1.claim: The idolaters worshiped idols as means of drawing near to God, since a rational person would not think lifeless stone independently benefits or harms; commoners' beliefs vary without limit.

JISHUMI:v8p6037/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6037/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6037/r2.claim: Another view is that the idolaters believed their idols themselves could bring benefit and harm.

JISHUMI:v8p6037/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6037/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6037/r3.claim: Creation in truth means God created for truth rather than falsehood, contrary to determinists who attribute every falsehood to God's creation, will, and decree.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r1.claim: Rolling night over day means one covers the other.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r2.claim: Another view says one enters the other.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r3.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r3.claim: Night decreases as day increases and vice versa; extremes are nine and fifteen hours. Takwīr means wrapping or gathering, as with a turban.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p108#2/r4.claim: Sun and moon are governed, each running to an appointed term.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r3.claim: Creation in truth means creation that is proper, realized, and fitted to its purposes and benefits.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r4.claim: Yukawwir describes night and day wrapping over one another, like layers of a turban: the longer covers part of the shorter and the shorter enters the longer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says yukawwir and yūliju mean the same; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this reports rather than properly explains the wording, which he treats as opposites.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r6.claim: The sun's subjection means that it continues its course in the ordered manner God wills.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p518#2/r7.claim: The appointed term may be the Resurrection, daily setting, or the moon's monthly and sun's yearly return to their courses.

TABRISI:39:4-5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:4-5/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:4-5/r3.claim: The heavens and earth were created for a wise purpose, not in vain; day and night progressively cover one another through increase and decrease, according to Hasan and other commentators.

TABRISI:39:4-5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:4-5/r4.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:39:4-5/r4.claim: Qatada interprets the alternation as covering one another or one entering the other, citing Quranic parallels.

TABRISI:39:4-5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:4-5/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:4-5/r5.claim: The sun and moon follow a regular course to an appointed limit, which may mean the end God set for them, the Resurrection, or a known seasonal rising and setting time.

TABRISI:39:4-5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:4-5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:4-5/r6.claim: The one capable of creating and governing the heavens, earth, sun, and moon is not in need of a child or partner; the verse demonstrates His power and freedom from need.

RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r1.claim: The passage follows the claim that God is one and dominant with signs of His power and self-sufficiency, then answers idolaters by describing attributes that constitute divinity.

RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r2.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth is an astronomical sign of a powerful God, with fuller proof discussed under another verse.

RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r3.claim: The alternation of night and day shows both light and darkness are overcome in turn and therefore subject to a stronger ruler; one grows as the other diminishes.

RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r4.claim: Takwir means the increasing of one period by the amount the other decreases; a prophetic phrase uses the same root for decline after prosperity.

RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r5.claim: A prophetic supplication seeks refuge from al-ḥawr after al-kawr, meaning reversal or decline after a period of gaining and advancing.

RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r6.claim: Other verses describe the same night-day relation as covering, interpenetration, or alternating succession.

RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r7.claim: The sun rules the day and the moon the night, and most benefits of the world depend on them.

RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r8.claim: Their appointed term is the Day of Resurrection; they continue until then and disappear, as another verse says the sun and moon are joined.

RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p212#2/r9.claim: Their subjection means that the celestial spheres move in a fixed orbit until the Resurrection, when the sky will be folded like a scroll.

RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r2.claim: The Sunni argument from “how are you turned away?” is that people were turned from the evidence by an agent other than themselves, namely God; reason supports this because people seek truth but end in error.

RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v26p214#2/r3.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that “how are you turned away?” expresses amazement, which would make no sense if God were the one turning them away.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r1.claim: Creating the heavens and earth in truth shows God's complete power and independence from spouse or child; such a Lord alone deserves worship and may prescribe what worship He wills.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r2.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r2.claim: Takwīr means casting one thing over another, as when something is rolled or piled upon something else.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r3.claim: What is reduced from night enters the day, and what is reduced from day enters the night, as in the verse about their interpenetration.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r4.claim: Night rolls over day by covering and removing its light, and day covers night to remove its darkness.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r5.claim: God subjugates the sun and moon in their rising and setting for people's benefit.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r6.claim: One view says their appointed term ends with the world's dissolution at Resurrection, when heaven splits and stars scatter.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r7.claim: Another view identifies the term as the endpoint of the sun and moon's ordered stations for setting and rising.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r8.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r8.claim: They travel to their farthest stations, then return to the nearest, never exceeding those limits.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:5-6/r9.claim: Alā is an alert; al-ʿazīz means the prevailing One and al-ghaffār the One who covers creatures' sins through mercy.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:4-5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:4-5/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:4-5/r3.claim: God rolls night over day and day over night, concealing one with the other like clothing wrapped around its wearer or a wrapped object, or making them follow in recurrent courses.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r1.claim: The sun and moon each run to a fixed endpoint, either the end of its cycle or the cessation of its motion.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:5-6/r2.claim: God is mighty over every possible thing and all things; delaying punishment preserves the mercy and general benefit in these creations.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p47#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p47#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p47#3/r1.claim: Takwīr is wrapping or winding, like wrapping a turban; night and day successively conceal one another from sight.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p47#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p47#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p47#3/r2.claim: The sun and moon are appointed to run until Judgment Day.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p47#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p47#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p47#3/r3.claim: God's might punishes those who fail to infer the Creator from the sun and moon, while He forgives those who reflect and believe in their governor.

QASHANI:39:5-6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:5-6/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:5-6/r1.claim: God creates by manifesting in forms and veiling through them, while governing all; the sun and moon’s subjection proves that no other has independent essence, quality, or act.

QASHANI:39:5-6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:5-6/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:5-6/r2.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the one who subdues all by power; al-Ghaffār either veils creation in His own light or covers the existence and qualities of whoever He wills.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r2.claim: The ordered creation of the upper and lower worlds, alternation of night and day, and regulated sun and moon demonstrate God's unity and dominion.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r3.claim: “A fixed term” may be the Resurrection, when the world's structure collapses, or their daily setting and rising, or the moon's phases each month.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r4.claim: Takwir means extending one over the other, as though the one partly covers its counterpart.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the alternation as night being carried over day.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r6.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says the increase of one is introduced through the decrease of the other.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r7.claim: Abu ʿUbayda simply says one enters into the other.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers images of one replacing the other like clothing, hiding it from sight, or rolling on in successive coils like a turban.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p184/r9.claim: Al-ʿAziz cannot be overcome; al-Ghaffar forgives penitents, or the name metaphorically describes God's patient forbearance.

SAMIN-DURR:39:5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:5/r1.claim: The تكور clause is most clearly an independent statement; Abu al-Baqa's circumstantial parse is weak because the event follows creation unless treated as a prospective state.

SAMIN-DURR:39:5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:5/r2.claim: التكوير means wrapping or rolling; night and day replace or cover one another like clothing, conceal each other, or roll over each other repeatedly, the last best matching the root according to al-Zamakhshari.

SAMIN-DURR:39:5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:5/r3.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:39:5/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines تكوير as rotation and gathering, and reads the verse as the sun's course and the lengthening and shortening of night and day; he also lists related senses for horses, bees, a travel saddle, and a district.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r1.claim: God created and owns everything in heaven and earth, and makes night and day follow each other rapidly, as Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, and al-Suddī explain.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p86/r2.claim: The sun and moon run until a term known to God, ending at the Resurrection; He is mighty yet forgiving to those who repent and return to Him.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r4.claim: The heavens and earth were brought from nonexistence in truth, perfectly and without flaw, variation, or disorder.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r5.claim: The repeated covering of night and day demonstrates divine power and subjugation even more strongly than the image of one entering the other.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r6.claim: Takwīr depicts night rapidly wrapping over and covering day, then day covering night; each replaces and conceals the other in a repeated cycle.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p419/r7.claim: The alternation also includes each light period lengthening as it takes time from the other, like clothing wrapped over what it covers.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r1.claim: The ordering of night before day follows the order of creation, since darkness precedes the light of sunrise.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r2.claim: God subdued the sun and moon, compelling each to follow its known course and fixed limit without benefit to the objects themselves.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r3.claim: Both bodies run by God's irrevocable decree, and their courses illustrate alternating human states of contraction and expansion, cognition and ignorance.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r4.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r4.claim: Al-Qushayrī maps the sky's cycles onto spiritual states: reason, knowledge, and recognition wax like stars, moons, and suns, while unity and connection alternate with doubt and separation.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r5.claim: The appointed term is the endpoint of each orbit and motion; specifying the governing decree emphasizes God's domination more than naming an endpoint alone.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p420/r6.claim: God alone is mighty; His repeated forgiveness explains why He delays seizing sinners, while He may erase their sins inwardly and outwardly or punish them by His might.

BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r1.claim: The verse points to the sun’s course through its risings and to the waxing and waning of night and day.

BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r2.claim: Night and day successively cover one another like clothing; alternatively, light and darkness conquer daily, disappear as if wrapped, or coil over each other like a turban.

BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r3.claim: God made the sun and moon obedient; each moves in its course for a fixed term, perhaps a daily or monthly cycle or until motion ceases at the Resurrection, for human benefit.

BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r4.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r4.claim: A hadith says seven angels are assigned to throw snow at the sun; without them, it would burn everything it struck.

BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p54#2/r5.claim: Ishari reading: two groups of believers receive light differently—one through striving and guidance, another through primordial grace and the light of knowledge.

BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r1.claim: God is dominant and able to punish sinners, yet greatly forgiving; He delays punishment and does not withdraw the benefits of creation despite people’s idolatry and sins.

BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r2.speaker: الغزالي
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r2.claim: Al-Ghazali explains al-Ghaffar as displaying beauty and concealing ugliness; God hides bodily defects, inward evil thoughts, and sins, promising to replace sins with good deeds for those who die in faith.

BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r3.claim: A servant’s share in this name is to conceal others’ faults as he wants his own concealed; a hadith promises God will conceal the fault of one who covers a believer’s flaw.

BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r4.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r4.claim: The Prophet said that whoever conceals a believer’s private fault will have his own fault concealed by God on Resurrection Day.

BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r5.claim: Backbiters, spies, and retaliators are far from this quality; one shares it by overlooking faults and mentioning only people’s good qualities, as every creature has both good and bad.

BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r6.speaker: عيسى
BURSEVI:v8p54#3/r6.claim: When disciples called a dead dog foul-smelling, Jesus pointed out its beautiful white teeth, teaching them to mention what is best in each thing.

BURSEVI:v8p54/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p54/r1.claim: Creation of the heavens, earth, and everything between them is by truth: it contains purposes and benefits rather than being futile or meaningless.

BURSEVI:v8p54/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p54/r2.claim: Kashifi says every created thing contains countless signs of power and wisdom, inviting observers to read the Creator’s proofs through reflection.

BURSEVI:v8p54/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p54/r3.claim: A Persian couplet likens the sky and earth to pages written with the admonition, ‘Take heed, people of insight.’

BURSEVI:v8p54/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54/r4.speaker: تاج المصادر
BURSEVI:v8p54/r4.claim: Taj al-Masadir glosses تكوير الليل على النهار as covering the day with night; it can also mean increasing one within the other.

BURSEVI:v8p54/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p54/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p54/r5.claim: Al-Raghib defines تكوير as turning and joining one part of a thing to another, as in winding a turban.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r1.claim: Creation in truth establishes the unity and sovereign power already mentioned; the world is made with wisdom and benefits.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r10.claim: The covering sense echoes the description of night and day as succeeding one another for remembrance.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r11.claim: The addition sense echoes the oath by the night that covers and the day that shines.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r12.claim: The successive-pursuit sense echoes the description of night covering day in rapid pursuit; several kinds of metaphor or simile are possible, with representation the best fit.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r13.claim: The imperfect verb indicates continuing renewal.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r2.claim: The clauses about night and day explain how God governs the created world, whose alternation depends on celestial bodies moving.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r3.claim: Takwīr originally means wrapping or winding, as one winds a turban around the head.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r4.claim: Qatāda explains the verse as one of night and day covering the other.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r5.claim: On the covering interpretation, one withdraws and the other covers its place, turning it dark or bright; the place may be the literal thing covered or the two periods may be personified.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r6.claim: Another explanation compares one period's disappearance when the other arrives to an object wrapped over something and hidden from sight.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r7.claim: A further reading is their repeated successive circling, like layers of a turban; it is called strongest because it combines wrapping and recurrence.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in reports from al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, explains one period as carrying the other by adding portions, lengthening one and shortening the other.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p238#2/r9.claim: The sense of carrying one into the other is clear and resembles the verse saying God inserts night into day and day into night.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r1.claim: The metaphor of forgiveness for withholding punishment is stronger and better than the proposed metonymy.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives both explanations of al-ʿAzīz al-Ghaffār: actual forgiveness of repentant sinners or power restrained through forbearance.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that the first reading should be abandoned as Muʿtazilite; God may forgive others too, while mentioning repentance best fits the context.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r4.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r4.claim: Al-Kashf says the first explanation suits creation in truth: perfect power and mercy warrant punishment for obstinacy and forgiveness for repentance.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r5.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r5.claim: Al-Kashf also links the first explanation to the passage's rejection of shirk: creation and revelation establish worship and sincere devotion, and the ending encourages seeking forgiveness while warning of disbelief and sin.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r6.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r6.claim: Al-Ṭībī prefers the second contextual correspondence, in which the ending intensifies condemnation of the shirk and divine offspring attributed to God.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239#2/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the first explanation's broader fit stronger; the chapter centers on worship, sincerity, and warning against unbelief and sins.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r1.claim: God subjected the sun and moon and made them obedient to His command.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r2.claim: Each luminary runs until its orbital cycle ends or its motion ceases.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r3.claim: The verse proves that the sun moves; al-Ālūsī criticizes claims that it is stationary and the world's center, including a recent European claim that it moves around another center.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r4.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the One able to punish those who persist in unbelief.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r5.claim: Al-Ghaffār forgives the sins of those who repent.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p239/r6.claim: A second explanation calls God conquering and able to punish, yet describes His postponement of punishment as forgiveness by a metaphor based on their shared feature of withholding.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p327/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p327/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p327/r6.claim: The creation of the heavens and earth explains God's oneness and irresistible power, and establishes that He alone creates, since the alleged partners cannot create the worlds.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r1.claim: Bi-l-ḥaqq means creation is joined to truth and wisdom, against purposelessness, with soundness and benefit rather than disorder.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r2.claim: The present tense yūkawwir suggests repeated renewal or evokes the action through its recurring effects, since the process itself is unseen.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r3.claim: Takwīr literally means wrapping; the alternation of night and day over earth is pictured as successive folds of a turban, with earth as the head.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r4.claim: Because takwīr derives from a round ball, Ibn ʿĀshūr reads the wording as a scientific allusion to Earth's sphericity, unknown to Arabs and most people then.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p328/r5.claim: The choice of takwīr suits this proof of divinity through creation and anticipates later Muslim astronomy; 7:54 instead uses ‘cover’ to show God's broad control over created qualities.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r1.claim: The phrase about rolling day over night is a coordinated part of the intended assertion, like the paired description in 66:5.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r2.claim: Subjugating the sun and moon means directing their ordered courses; this is coordinated because the day-night alternation results from that subjugation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r3.claim: ‘Each runs for a term’ is an inclusive apposition clarifying the subjugation; kull is compensatory for ‘each one,’ and running means swift movement.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r4.claim: The term may be the end of the sun and moon: their motion advances their eventual extinction, as with the sun's course to its resting place.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r5.claim: Alternatively, the term may be human lifespans, measured by the periods and breaths tracked through the sun and moon's motion.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r6.speaker: أسقف نجران
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r6.claim: A bishop of Najran's verse uses the sun's changing course as evidence against permanence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p329/r7.claim: Al-ajl al-musammā is what God marked out; ‘for a term’ and ‘to a term’ are close in basic meaning, and the differing prepositions may simply vary the expression.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r1.claim: Al-ʿAzīz warns that God does what He wills and cannot be overcome; al-Ghaffār invites repentance through Islam, especially before death ends the chance to repent.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p330/r2.claim: Mentioning forgiveness alongside the appointed term urges people to repent before death, when recovery is no longer possible; the opening alert marks the statement's importance.

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r1.claim: Both verses establish exclusive lordship by joining creation and governance: pagans accept one Creator but multiply lords, while governance remains part of creation.

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r2.claim: The phrase creation in truth means creation is purposeful rather than vain, and its intended end entails resurrection.

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r3.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines takwīr as laying one thing over another; here it depicts night and day continuously succeeding one another.

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r4.claim: The sun and moon are subjected to the world's order and run within it until a fixed term they do not exceed.

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r5.claim: The names Mighty and Forgiving may support exclusive lordship: only the invincible and the true forgiver merits worship.

TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the names exhort people to believe in the one God, take pride in His might, and seek His forgiveness.

TABATABAI:39:5-6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:5-6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:5-6/r7.claim: Creation in truth may indicate God's creative governance and power, but the connection to the next verse makes it an argument for His exclusive lordship.

ASAD-NOTES:39:5#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:5#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:5#n5/r1.claim: Asad points to his note on 10:5 for the phrase describing creation in truth.

ASAD-NOTES:39:5#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:5#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:5#n6/r1.claim: Asad points to his explanation at 13:2 for the sun and moon's appointed course.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r1.claim: Verses 5–8 describe purposeful creation and cosmic order, establishing God as sole Creator and Lord and human dependence on Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p526/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p526/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p526/r5.claim: Purposeful creation requires truth and falsehood, virtue and vice to be judged separately; otherwise the world would be meaningless and intercession could falsely guarantee status.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r1.claim: God continuously governs the world: He alternates day and night, serves humanity through the sun and moon, and keeps celestial bodies on fixed schedules.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p527/r2.claim: God is both mighty and forgiving: His might bars unauthorized intercession, while He Himself forgives those worthy of forgiveness.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r5.claim: The night/day wording describes light gradually withdrawing as night arrives and darkness gradually yielding as day begins.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r6.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r6.claim: Another interpretation is that God adds night to day and day to night.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r7.claim: The recurring daily transitions are signs of divine power and of the continuing manifestation of wisdom in creation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:5/r8.claim: The sun and moon obey God's laws, beautify the sky, and provide heat and light.

STUDYQURAN:39:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:5/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:5/r1.claim: Creation in truth is reiterated elsewhere; here it is linked to revelation in verse 2, suggesting revelation and creation share an underlying reality and creation is God’s first revelation.

STUDYQURAN:39:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:5/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:5/r2.claim: Rolling day into night and night into day is expressed elsewhere as night passing into day and day into night.

STUDYQURAN:39:5/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:5/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:5/r3.claim: The sun and moon’s subservience shows their reality remains determined by the truth of their creation and evokes the dominion and responsibility God gives human vicegerents.
